requirements.requirement: Existing data under /srv/inventory owned by inventorysvc
requirements.summary: chown -R inventorysvc:inventory-readers applied to /srv/inventory and confirmed via ls -ld and post-restart getent/ls checks showing inventorysvc as owner on all files and directories.
Directories set to 750 and files to 640 with group inventory-readers; a test user added to inventory-readers successfully read records.csv, confirming group read access works end-to-end.
A test user not in inventory-readers or owning the files received Permission denied on both ls and cat against /srv/inventory, directly confirming the 750/640 permissions block outside access.

Original file contents were read via cat before any permission changes; only chown/chmod commands were run (no writes to file contents), and post-restart md5sums matched the pre-restart baseline, indicating no content changes occurred during the repair.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task contract — ownership by inventorysvc, group-read access for inventory-readers, exclusion of other users, and preservation of existing data contents — are directly and coherently demonstrated by executor evidence, including a live access-control test with dedicated reader/other test accounts. The independently mandated node-restart evidence protocol was also fully satisfied: a pre-restart boot_id and data baseline, an acknowledged reboot, a distinct post-restart boot_id, and a post-restart re-verification of ownership, permissions, and identical data checksums, corroborated by the fixed before/after lifecycle snapshots showing the boot-identity change and no other unexplained system drift.
limitations: Post-restart data preservation was verified via md5sum comparison against a baseline taken after the chown/chmod repair, not against the original pre-repair sha256 hashes recorded during prepare; preservation of the original content itself relies on the absence of any write commands rather than a direct hash match to the prepare-stage baseline.
A minor residual file /tmp/reboot.log from the reboot invocation was left on node1 and not cleaned up, though it is low-risk and unrelated to the managed application state.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor created and fully removed two temporary test accounts (readertest, othertest) solely to validate the access-control outcome, which is a legitimate, bounded verification step and was confirmed reverted via getent (cmd-41e5ba8aeb054686, cmd-c1d2a564bb564492). The nohup reboot command left a small residue file /tmp/reboot.log that was not cleaned up (visible in after_executor temporary-files diff), a minor uncleaned artifact from the restart action rather than an unnecessary mutation. No other unexplained mutations, failed services, or unsafe exposures were observed; listening-sockets and package-health are unchanged aside from expected boot-related PID/address churn.
